newsitem.title: UK: Britain's First Leisure boosts profits.
newsitem.headline: Britain's First Leisure boosts profits.

text.p: Britain's First Leisure Corp Plc reported a nine percent rise in annual profit on Thursday and said heavy investment in expansion would bear fruit in the next few years.
First Leisure, which operates nightclubs, fitness centres and bingo clubs, plans to invest some 100 million pounds ($170 million) on new venues over the next 18 months or so.
"We will see the fruits of our strategy coming through over the next three years," said chief executive John Conlan.

Pre-tax profit for the year to end October 1996 rose by nine percent to 43.7 million pounds on turnover of 183 million, up by 15 percent. The profit was boosted by a 1.6 million pound gain on the sale of the company's snooker businesses.
First Leisure shares added 4p to 348.5p on the back of results which were at the top end of expectations.
Strong performances were reported from the company's three main divisions, nightclubs and bars, sports and resorts, profits growing by 15 percent and more in all three areas.
First Leisure's operations include attractions in seaside resorts, including the Blackpool Tower in north-west England.
One disappointment was Bingo, the traditional numbers game which has been badly hit by competition from Britain's National Lottery since its launch two years ago.
First Leisure has been developing modern bingo halls under the "Riva" brand name and is convinced that the industry has a future once it is deregulated.
Conlan said that he hoped legislation would be approved fairly quickly to lift restrictions on bingo advertising and "restore a level playing field" with the lottery.

"That will enable the industry to get back the volume lost over the last 18 months or so," Conlan said, saying that bingo was a billion pound business which had been reliable for generations and could still thrive.
"We're going to stick with it," he said, nothing that bingo was only a small part of the group's activity.
